Neural networks have risen and fallen in popularity three times,
under three names [@goodfellow2016deep, section 1.2.1]:

::: {.ruled-rows}

| Years | Name | Milestones |
|-------|------|------------|
| 1940s to 1960s | Cybernetics | A logical model of a neuron [@mcculloch1943logical]; the perceptron, which learned its weights from examples [@rosenblatt1958perceptron] |
| 1980s to 1990s | Connectionism | Backpropagation for networks with hidden layers [@rumelhart1986learning]; convolutional networks reading handwritten zip codes [@lecun1989backpropagation] |
| 2006 on | [Deep learning](#def-deep-learning) | Deep belief networks, trained one layer at a time [@hinton2006fast]; AlexNet [@krizhevsky2012imagenet]; the Transformer [@vaswani2017attention] |

: The three waves of neural network research.

:::

The first wave faded after @minsky1969perceptrons showed that a perceptron,
which has no hidden layer,
cannot compute some simple functions of its inputs,
such as the exclusive or of two binary inputs.
Networks with hidden layers can,
and backpropagation, one result of the second wave, trained them
[@rumelhart1986learning; @goodfellow2016deep, section 1.2.1].
